name: Security Headers & CSP Builder
summary: Compose Content-Security-Policy and the other security headers for common servers, and grade a pasted policy with the fix for each weakness.
about: Composes a Content-Security-Policy per CSP Level 3, plus HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy, and writes the same header values out for Apache, nginx, Netlify's _headers file and a plain generic list. Every value passes a single-line safety check before any output is built, so a pasted line break or control character can never start a second header or a server directive. A pasted Content-Security-Policy can also be graded: with Grade this policy ticked, the page gives a grade and a score from 24 stated rules and lists each weakness with its severity, the directive, why it matters and the fix, every rule tied to a section of W3C Content Security Policy Level 3 or marked as this page's own rule.
supports: CSP Level 3 directive and source-list grammar: keyword, scheme, host, nonce and hash source expressions, with line-numbered problems for an unknown directive, a duplicate, 'none' combined with another source, an unquoted keyword or a source that does not match the grammar
upgrade-insecure-requests, added to the CSP header text (it is defined by the Mixed Content specification, not CSP Level 3 itself)
HSTS max-age and includeSubDomains per RFC 6797, with preload refused unless the hstspreload.org submission requirements (includeSubDomains and a one-year minimum max-age) are met
Referrer-Policy, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy restricted to each specification's own defined token list
Permissions-Policy written as an RFC 9651 structured-field dictionary, with * for every origin, () for none, and an allowlist of self and quoted origins
The same header set rendered for Apache (mod_headers), nginx (add_header), Netlify's _headers file and a plain Name: value list
A value carrying a line break or control character refused before any target is written, naming the field and position

Grading a pasted policy (the Grade this policy box, off by default): 24 rules in four severities (high, medium, low and info), each reading the source list that governs it through the CSP Level 3 section 6.8.3 fallback order, so the most specific of script-src-elem, script-src and default-src alone decides

A pasted header line, a Report-Only header line or a meta element, read as its policy and graded with a note of what was taken off; the headers built above use the same text, so the header name is not reported as an unknown directive
Policies that use 'strict-dynamic': the host, scheme and wildcard rules stay quiet and the ignored sources are reported instead, as CSP Level 3 section 8.2 describes
Findings listed by severity and then by rule order, each with the directive, what is wrong, why it matters, the fix and the section it rests on
limits: This tool does not run Apache, nginx or Netlify itself, so it cannot tell whether the relevant module is enabled or whether another rule on the real server overrides these headers; the configuration cannot be tested without a real server
A strict policy can break inline scripts, inline styles and third-party embeds on the visitor's own site; this tool checks the grammar, not whether the policy matches what the site actually needs
X-Frame-Options and Trusted Types headers are not generated; use the CSP frame-ancestors directive for frame embedding control instead

Apache values have every percent sign doubled and nginx values refuse a dollar sign outright, because each server's own config-file parser gives that character special meaning; this tool does not attempt every possible escaping trick beyond what each server's own documentation describes
Grading follows the rules listed on the page, each tied to a section of W3C Content Security Policy Level 3 or marked as this page's own rule.
The grade is this page's summary (high 30, medium 15 and low 5 points off 100; any high finding caps it at D); it is not a statement that a policy is secure.
Policies of up to 64 KiB (65,536 characters) are graded; a longer one is refused for grading.

A rule that applies takes its points once, however many findings it lists; the script rules read the list that governs script elements (script-src-elem, then script-src, then default-src), and script-src-attr, worker-src and the other fetch directives are not graded one by one
A policy is read as pasted, with one directive per line or separated by semicolons; several policies joined by commas, and other response headers around a pasted line, are not read
ambiguities: A directive this tool does not recognise (an unknown name, or a fetch directive an earlier CSP version removed) is reported with its line and dropped from the built header text, since re-emitting an unrecognised directive verbatim could not be checked for safety either
A Permissions-Policy feature name outside the standardised list this tool checked is a warning, not an error, because browsers ship feature names beyond that list

Graders weigh rules differently, so the same policy can get another letter elsewhere; this page's letter only summarises the rules it lists, and a pasted policy that is not enforced (a Report-Only header or a meta element missing directives) is graded as written

standards.label: CSP Level 3 — Content Security Policy Level 3
Fetch Standard — X-Content-Type-Options and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy headers
HTML Living Standard — Cross-origin opener and embedder policies
RFC 9651 — Structured Field Values for HTTP
RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics, section 5.5 Field Values

apiNotes: `buildSecurityHeaders` throws `SecurityHeadersError` (fields `field`, `line`) for a value a single header cannot carry safely or an option outside a specification's defined token list; CSP grammar problems are reported as line-numbered warnings instead, since a browser ignores an unrecognised directive rather than rejecting the whole policy. `gradeCsp` reads text only and returns `{ grade, score, findings, source, policy, empty, notes }`; it throws `CspGradeError` for a policy over 65,536 characters, and an `empty` result carries no grade.
testNotes: CSP source-list grammar is checked against the ABNF fetched from CSP Level 3's own "Source Lists" section; HSTS against RFC 6797 sections 6.1 and 8.1 plus the hstspreload.org submission requirements; each token-list header against its own specification's defined values; Permissions-Policy serialisation against RFC 9651 sections 4.1.1.1 and 4.1.6; Apache and nginx escaping against each server's own fetched documentation and, for nginx, its own config-file tokenizer source. The grading rules are checked on the example policies CSP Level 3 prints itself (the section 8.5 strict policies, the section 8.2 compatibility policy, the section 8.6 exfiltration policy and the section 6.7.3.2 source lists), on a policy built for each of the 24 rules, and on a 64 KiB paste in twelve shapes that must be graded in under a second.
